name: vLLM
tagline: High-throughput and memory-efficient LLM inference and serving engine
summary: vLLM is a high-throughput and memory-efficient LLM serving engine designed to maximize GPU utilization through PagedAttention. It radically reduces memory waste in the KV cache, enabling significantly higher serving throughput compared to traditional inference stacks.
verdict: An essential open-source utility for any team looking to self-host and scale LLM inference efficiently in production without incurring massive cloud overhead.

key_features.title: PagedAttention Memory Management
key_features.description: Virtualizes attention keys and values to eliminate memory fragmentation and reduce KV cache waste.

key_features.title: Seamless Hugging Face Integration

use_cases: Deploying a high-concurrency LLM API endpoint for production web apps
Serving open-source foundation models like Llama or Mistral on self-hosted GPU clusters
Optimizing throughput to reduce operational inference costs for enterprise AI agents
pros: Dramatically higher serving throughput than standard Hugging Face Transformers pipeline
Significantly lower GPU memory footprint via innovative PagedAttention algorithm
Extensive out-of-the-box model architecture support and active open-source community
cons: Complex codebase can make deep custom kernel modifications challenging
Rapid release cycle occasionally introduces integration regressions for niche hardware
target_audience: ML engineers and backend developers building production-grade LLM applications and self-hosted APIs
comparison_vs_alt: Unlike Triton, vLLM is purpose-built specifically for large language models with native optimizations like PagedAttention, offering simpler Python-centric configuration and superior out-of-the-box token generation throughput.
